limitations: Original-game callees are deterministic stubs: the wrapped function returns a fixed value and the two native revenge functions plus the squad helper are stubs whose return the case controls.  What is proven is our contribution and the call/ABI contract.
Executed paths only; Windows unwind and native gameplay are not executed.
The battle-unit table, unit records and action context are synthetic fixtures.
The revenge wrapper is entered from its one static call site; the pair is asserted by the call edges it makes, not by observing the game's status record.
The steal family's effect is the caller-visible esi; the victim-eligibility callee is stubbed, so the item transfer it gates is not executed.
Build-only is fixture/patch validation, not an emulator pass.
